learn.explainer: A botnet is a group of devices controlled together through malicious software. In this story, Android TV boxes were used to rent users’ internet connections as proxies.
AI agents are software systems designed to carry out tasks. Saab says its academy will develop agents and infrastructure to create, train and evaluate them for future aircraft projects.

A peacekeeping mission is an operation described as working to support peace in a particular place. The story says the Western Sahara mission ended after an impasse between the US and Russia at the UN.

analysis.headline: Disruption, oversight and contested security
paragraphs: The stories point to different forms of control and accountability. Google and industry partners say they dismantled a botnet using Android TV boxes, while the AI article raises questions about who sets the terms for oversight. Both make visibility into systems and their operators a central concern.

For defenders, the botnet story is a reminder to examine devices that may be treated as ordinary household or network equipment. The AI discussion suggests that human oversight and scrutiny of developers matter in security and defense. These stories do not establish that the same risks or responses apply across both settings.

Other top stories describe a Russian bombing reported by Ukrainian officials and the end of a Western Sahara peacekeeping mission after a US-Russia impasse at the UN. Analysts can watch how claims are attributed, what oversight or institutional roles are described, and how security developments intersect with political decisions.
takeaways: Check connected devices for unexpected network behavior.
Keep human oversight and scrutiny in view when assessing AI systems.
Separate reported claims from confirmed details in conflict and geopolitical coverage.
